review.summary: The design draft does not align with the mandatory 2026 'LOUD' visual identity. Please revise the color palette, remove grain textures, and update the typography to meet brand standards.

flags.issue: The draft uses a retired pastel orange and muted green palette instead of the required electric 'LOUD' identity colors.
flags.suggestion: Replace the current palette with the approved high-contrast colors: electric orange, acid lime, hot pink, and black.

citations.quote: love. only note: that lilac tag in the corner is a leftover from the old system. swap it to hot pink.
citations.author: Jess Okafor

citations.quote: Rebrand brief from Theo Lindqvist (Founder & CEO) and Jess Okafor (Head of Brand): We are rebranding. The soft pastel look got copied by every D2C snack brand and we are invisible on shelf. New direction is LOUD: electric orange #FF5A1F, acid lime #C6F432 and hot pink #FF3EA5 on black #0D0D0D. Chunky condensed type, all-caps headlines are allowed now. The energy of a mosh pit, not a candle shop. Kill the grain texture and the faded colour grading. The old pastel palette (sage, peach, lilac, oat) is retired. Jess added: "yes, this means neon is ok now lol. i know i said never."
citations.author: Theo Lindqvist

observations: [Colour] Crunchd brand identity requires a 'LOUD' visual identity using electric orange #FF5A1F, acid lime #C6F432, hot pink #FF3EA5, and black #0D0D0D, superseding the previous soft pastel palette (sage, peach, lilac, oat) as of 2026-06-02. As of 2026-07-20, the use of lilac tags is explicitly prohibited as a legacy element, with hot pink preferred for design accents; this preference was confirmed by the approval of the 'Mango Habanero' post on 2026-07-21.

flags.issue: The draft includes film grain and noise texture, which is prohibited under the new brand guidelines.
flags.suggestion: Remove all grain texture and vintage grading to achieve a crisp, punchy, and high-contrast look.

citations.quote: Drop the grain and the vintage grade. Crisp, punchy, high contrast. The faded look is the old brand.

evidence.text: [Imagery] Crunchd brand identity prohibits grain texture and faded color grading as of 2026-06-02, as part of the new 'LOUD' visual identity; as of 2026-06-18, Theo Lindqvist explicitly requires designs to be crisp, punchy, and high contrast, specifically rejecting any remaining grain or vintage photo grading in the 'Rebrand reveal post' (project cr-08).

[Colour] Crunchd brand identity requires a 'LOUD' visual identity using electric orange #FF5A1F, acid lime #C6F432, hot pink #FF3EA5, and black #0D0D0D, superseding the previous soft pastel palette (sage, peach, lilac, oat) as of 2026-06-02. As of 2026-07-20, the use of lilac tags is explicitly prohibited as a legacy element, with hot pink preferred for design accents; this preference was confirmed by the approval of the 'Mango Habanero' post on 2026-07-21.

[Compliance] Crunchd brand identity requires that designs avoid blending in with other content; as of 2026-06-02, the brand has adopted a 'LOUD' visual identity to ensure visibility on shelf, replacing the previous soft pastel look which was deemed too generic.
[Imagery] Crunchd brand identity allows the use of one emoji per slide in carousel-style design assets, as approved for the 'Carousel: ingredients we don't use' project on 2025-09-12.

[Typography] Crunchd brand identity requires chunky condensed type and permits all-caps headlines to reflect a mosh pit energy, as of 2026-06-02; as of 2026-06-15, condensed caps typography is specifically required for the 'Rebrand reveal post' to achieve a 'louder' brand aesthetic, which was confirmed by the approval of the final design on 2026-06-22.
[Typography] Handwritten script is prohibited for use in design assets because it is unreadable at thumbnail size.
[Layout] Instagram post images must contain a maximum of one line of text; all other copy must be placed in the caption.

[Layout] Crunchd brand identity requires that designs clearly communicate the product being sold, avoiding excessive minimalism that obscures the product identity; additionally, designs must avoid clutter and limit the amount of text used. As of 2025-07-14, this includes a specific requirement for the 'Brooklyn bus shelter poster' project that each poster must feature only one hero flavour with the flavour name displayed clearly and prominently, replacing the previous requirement of one flavour and one bag. This supersedes the earlier rejection of designs with multiple flavour names and multiple bags.
[Layout] Crunchd brand identity requires product shots to be positioned off-center to avoid a catalog-like appearance.
[Layout] Crunchd brand identity for the 'Back-to-school campus poster' requires an acid lime background, one bag image, and the flavour name in huge black condensed caps.

[Layout] Crunchd brand identity requires a maximum of one emoji per slide for the 'Carousel: ingredients we don't use' project to prevent visual clutter, replacing the previous draft's use of four to five emojis.
[Copy] Crunchd brand identity prohibits the use of the word 'ALERT' and triple exclamation marks to avoid an advertisement-like appearance.
